headline: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 2 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: After the opening ITT won by Tadej Pogacar with the narrowest margin, the peloton ride away from Monaco and head to France with a 202.1 km stage 2 from Monaco to Manosque, in France. The route is rolling, with no less than 3,020 metres of elevation and a slightly rising finale. Can versatile sprinters such as Mads Pedersen (who has already won in Manosque) survive the climbs of the day and battle for victory? The neutral start is set at 12, the start proper at 12:42 after a 21 km parade, and the winners should be crowned at around 17:30.

headline: From Monaco to Manosque
subtext: After yesterday’s ITT in the streets of Monaco, today marks the 12th Grand Tour stage starting from the Principality: 9 in the Tour de France, 2 in La Vuelta, 1 in the Giro. Tadej Pogacar won the last two Grand Tour stages starting from Monaco: stage 21 of the Tour 2024, stage 1 of La Vuelta 26. Both stages were ITTs. Manosque is a stage town for the first time in La Vuelta. It has been on the map of the Tour de France in 1976 and 1982. A classic venue for Paris-Nice, Manosque has also witnessed Tour de la Provence stage wins by Bryan Coquard (2022) and Mads Pedersen (2024, 2025). The finish line was on the Avenue de l’Argile, just like today’s. Monaco and Manosque open the list of towns making their first appearance at La Vuelta this year. They will be followed by Font-Romeu (stage 3), Falset (5), Roquetes (5), Vall d’Alba (7), Puçol (8), Xeraco (8), La Vila Joiosa (9), Alcaraz (10), Elche de la Sierra (10), Vera (12), Almuñécar (13), Palma del Rio (15), Cortegana (16), La Rábida (16), Dos Hermanas (17), El Puerto de Santa María (18), La Calahorra (20), and Collado del Aguacil (20).

headline: Happy birthday Tobias
subtext: Tobias Johannessen turns 27 today. He participates for the first time in La Vuelta, after four participations in the Tour de France (best result: 6th in 2025).

headline: Let’s roll
subtext: The peloton make their way to the start proper with a 21 km parade.

headline: La Roja
subtext: A winner of the Tour de France and the Giro, Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) has now led all three Grand Tours (71 Maillot Jaune, 20 Maglia Rosa, 1 La Roja). He follows in the footsteps of Jonas Vingegaard, who won the Giro d’Italia this year after previous success at the Tour de France and La Vuelta. The other two active riders to have worn La Roja, the Maillot Jaune and the Maglia Rosa are participating in La Vuelta 26: Primoz Roglic and Richard Carapaz. Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) is level on time with the Sloevnian. Joshua Tarling (Netcompany Ineos) trails by 4’’, and Callum Thornley (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) by 5.

headline: Green jersey
subtext: With his victory in the ITT, Tadej Pogacar also took 20 points. Since he races with La Roja, Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) will be wearing the green jersey today. He has 17 points. Joshua Tarling (Netcompany Ineos) follows with 15 points.

headline: White jersey
subtext: For the second year in a row, the first leader of the young riders standings is British, as Josh Tarling follows in the footsteps of Ethan Vernon. It was also the case in 2022, when Ethen Hayter took the first four white jerseys before handing it to Fred Wright for one day. This is Tarling’s first distinctive jersey in a Grand Tour.

headline: Team standings
subtext: With Tadej Pogacar (1st), Jay Vine (13th) and Ivo Oliveira (14th) in the first positions, UAE Emirates XRG had the best collective performance yesterday. They lead the team standings ahead of Visma-Lease a Bike (+3’’) and Decathlon CMA CGM (+7’’).

headline: A special day for Molard: "I have some lovely memories"
subtext: Rudy Molard (Groupama-FDJ United) lives in Tourette-sur-Loup, close to Nice, studied in Barcelonnette and raced around Manosque in the youth categories: “Today, you could say I’m the local rider for this stage, especially as the start is actually going to be very close to my home. We’ll be on my training routes during the first part of the stage. We’re heading into a department I know well, the 04 [Alpes-de-Haute-Provence]. I went to school in Barcelonnette and often travelled to Manosque with the UNSS [Union Nationale du Sport Scolaire] to take part in competitions. I have some lovely memories.” Now aged 36 (he will turn 37 the week after La Vuelta), Molard rides La Vuelta for the seventh time. He got to wear La Roja both in 2018 (4 stages) and in 2022 (1).

headline: Stage 2 is ON!
subtext: The start was slightly delayed as riders suffered mechanicals ahead of km 0.

headline: First attacks
subtext: Three riders rapidly opened a gap but they were immediately caught. Now two attackers are riding 17'' ahead of the bunch.

headline: 15 kilometres into the stage
subtext: The battle for the first breakaway of La Vuelta 26 goes on. We are experiencing technical difficulties and are working on resolving them to bring you the most accurate and complete coverage of the race.

headline: 2 leaders, Hayter and Fernandez in pursuit
subtext: After 25 kilometres of racing, Koen Bouwman (Jayco AlUla) and Diego Uriarte (Kern Pharma) lead the way. Second in GC, Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) is 15 seconds behing them. Then, Sinhué Fernandez (Burgos-Burpellet-BH) trails by 1'20''. Visma-Lease a Bike drives the bunch with a gap of 3'20''.

headline: Hayter makes it 3 leaders
subtext: Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) has now bridged the gap to the lead duo. Sinhué Fernandez (Burgos-Burpellet-BH) moves closer: 55 seconds. The gap to the bunch is down to 2'30''.

headline: Hayter and Van Aert already battling for La Roja
subtext: Beaten by the narrowest margin yesterday in Monaco (0.09 second), Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) is level on time with Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) in GC. His move in the first part of stage 2 means he now leads the virtual standings. And he likely has his mind set on the bonus sprint (km 166.2), where the first three riders will take 6, 4 and 2 seconds. Currently drving the bunch, Visma-Lease a Bike certainly don’t want Hayter to get there: Wout van Aert hopes he can take La Roja with the 10 bonus seconds awarded to the stage winner. Hayter gained 9 seconds on the Belgian star yesterday.

headline: The gaps decrease
subtext: Sinhué Fernandez (Burgos-Burpellet-BH) is 20 seconds behind the three leaders, while the peloton trail by 2 minutes.

headline: Results at Alto Châteauneuf-Grasse (km 32.3)
subtext: 1. Bouwman, 3 pts 2. Uriarte, 2 pts 3. Hayter, 1 pt The winner of the KOM standings at the Giro 2022, Koen Bouwman (Jayco AlUla) is set to chase the polka dots again.

headline: Fernandez also joins the break
subtext: Make it 4 leaders as the race visits Grasse, the hometown of Giblert Bellone, winner of stage 8 of La Vuelta in 1967. The peloton trail by 1'40''.

headline: 43.1 km in the first hour
subtext: And the battle goes on as Visma-Lease a Bike want to keep a tight leash on the four attackers, especially Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step).

headline: Passed km 50
subtext: The gap from the four leaders to the bunch is down to 1'35''.

headline: Van Aert eyes "a small chance to go for the red jersey"
subtext: Visma-Lease a Bike started pulling early today as they want to battle for the stage win and also ensure Wout van Aert is in a position to claim La Roja with the bonus seconds at the finish. “It was a nice take away yesterday to see that I was within ten seconds, it gives me a small chance to go for the red jersey”, the Belgian star said today at the start. “But on the other hand i hoped to be closer yesterday so we’ll see. The final should suit me, it looks pretty hard. The last couple of kilometres are always dragging up with a few steeper parts, it will be a sprint for strong men. It’s a nice final, a final that I like.” His plans are threatened by Ethan Hayter’s breakaway.

headline: The situation settles
subtext: At km 60, the peloton are 1'55'' behind Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step), Koen Bouwman (Jayco AlUla), Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) and Diego Uriarte (Kern Pharma).

headline: Pogacar: "I hope somebody from our team will win"
subtext: Tadej Pogacar enjoys his first day with La Roja and hopes a rider of UAE Emirates XRG can fend off Wout van Aert today at the finish: “It will be a memorable day. I will try to enjoy all the kilometres we have today in this beautiful jersey. [Wout van Aert] is at less than ten seconds and the finish has a ten seconds [bonus], it’s also a perfect sprint for him. It’s hard, so he can win and take the jersey. [But] I hope somebody from our team will win.”

headline: Tadej Pogacar in the red jersey
Some stats about Pogacar and his first day with La Roja
subtext: A winner of the Tour de France and the Giro, Pogacar has now led all three Grand Tours (71 Maillot Jaune, 20 Maglia Rosa, 1 La Roja). He follows in the footsteps of Jonas Vingegaard, who won the Giro d’Italia this year after previous success at the Tour de France and La Vuelta. The other two active riders to have worn La Roja, the Maillot Jaune and the Maglia Rosa are participating in La Vuelta 26: Primoz Roglic and Richard Carapaz. Pogacar had never led a Grand Tour so early. In 2024, he took the Maglia Rosa on stage 2 of the Giro, and then the Maillot Jaune on stage 2 of the Tour. Pogacar is the third Slovenian leader of La Vuelta after Janez Brajkovic and Primoz Roglic.

headline: A gap of 1'42'' at km 70
subtext: So far, the race scenario aligns with the predictions of Kaden Groves (Alpecin-Premier Tech): "It’s gonna be a hard stage, up and down, always sort of twisty roads. It’s a tough stage, especially the final, but I expect a small breakaway controlled by Visma to try and take the red jersey with Van Aert. I expect a bunch sprint but it’s a super hard final so you have to see how the legs are."

headline: Lidl-Trek pull the bunch with Visma-Lease a Bike
subtext: Mads Pedersen (Lidl-Trek) has two victories in Manosque at the Tour de la Provence: “[The finish] is uphill and uphill, it suits me really well so of course it gives some confidence to have won there twice, but you can’t compare La Vuelta and le Tour de la Provence, with all the respect for Provence. There are two different races, but I look forward to this stage.” Today's finish line is set on Avenue de l'Argile, like it usually is at the Tour de la Provence.

headline: The gap is decreasing
subtext: The peloton reach km 80 with a gap of 1'20''.

headline: Sinuhé Fernández joins Uriarte, Bouwman and Hayter at the front
Van Aert vs Pedersen? Their own words ahead of a potential duel
subtext: Is Mads Pedersen ready for a first battle with Wout van Aert? “For sure, and with many other riders who will be there. It’s a fresh start, people are ready and aiming to win as well. It’s gonna be a nice duel.” Van Aert: “It will probably be more complicated [than just beating Pedersen], but if you beat Mads in a finish like this, then you have a good chance. I expect him to be really strong.”

headline: The average speed after 2 hours: 42.6 km/h
subtext: The gap has stabilised again: 1'30''.

headline: Results at Col de Saint-Andrieu (km 92.4)
subtext: 1.Bouwman, 3 pts 2. Uriarte, 2 pts 3. Fernandez, 1 pt

headline: Bouwman all but secures the polka dots
subtext: With 6 KOM points, Koen Bouwman (Jayco AlUla) is set to be the first leader of the KOM standings of La Vuelta 26 if he reaches the finish without incidents. He will be the first Dutch leader of the KOM standings since Julius van den Berg, who similarly took the polka-dot jersey on day 2 of La Vuelta 22.

headline: Halfway through the stage
subtext: The four leaders enter the final 100 kilometres with a gap down to 1'10''.

headline: Kruijswijk and Mosca set the pace in the bunch
subtext: The gap is down to 1 minute with a little bit more than 90 kilometres remaining. The Netcompany Ineos riders are right behind Steven Kruijswijk (Visma-Lease a Bike) and Jacopo Mosca (Lidl-Trek).

headline: The peloton is controlling the breakaway's efforts
Turner: "A challenging day"
subtext: Positioned at the front of the peloton, Netcompany Ineos have a couple of cards to play today, as explained by Ben Turner: "It’s a nice stage, it’s going to be much harder than it looks on paper. I think it will be a sprint but it’s going to be a challenging day, it’s rolling all day so there will be a bit of fatigue already. I guess there are a few [similarities with the stage I won last year], there’s a longer climb. Let’s hope for good legs and try to make the most of the day. It’s good for both of us [with Axel Laurance], we have to see on the road a bit. Of course if there are more climb than sprint it’s better for him, we’re gonna see on the road and make the call. There is also a lot of road between now and the finish line so plenty of time.”

headline: 80 kilometres to go
subtext: The gap has stabilised at around 1 minute.

headline: Fisher-Black to “look for an opportunity”
subtext: After he finished 9th in yesterday’s ITT, Finn Fisher-Black (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) wants to make the most of the first few days ofLa Vuelta 26: “I was pretty happy [with yesterday’s ITT]. The legs felt super good. I was just a bit slower in the corners than the other guys so I lost a bit there, but I was really happy with how the body felt. There’s a bit more confidence coming into this Vuelta than last year’s, coming of Poland last week. I feel good so hopefully we can make something of this Vuelta. It would be nice. In the Vuelta, I want to go for stages. To win a stage here would be amazing, it would be a dream. I definitely thinking about any way that I can win today. There is definitely a few guys that are faster than me. So I have to look for an opportunity and see what I can do in the finale.”

headline: 45 seconds
subtext: Steven Kruijswijk (Visma-Lease a Bike) sets a strong pace with 75 kilometres to go.

headline: Langellotti: “Just an immense pleasure”
subtext: Monaco is now quite far behind the riders. But the Gran Salida 26 will forever be with Victor Langellotti (XDS Astana): “It was absolutely brilliant! I really had goosebumps when we set off from the casino. It felt really strange. Just an immense pleasure. I was so happy. I thoroughly enjoyed the whole time trial. I didn’t pay any attention to the data or anything like that. I was really focused on the line and simply giving it my all, so I’d have no regrets. All I’ll take away from this is immense pleasure and a dream come true. I’m going to show the others the way to the very top [of the Palais]. Joking aside, it’s just incredible. I can’t wait to see how things go at the Palais; I’m looking forward to seeing Monseigneur and counting on his support – it’s just unique. After the time trial, we managed to exchange a few words because he was following me in his car. It’s quite special, really, and I can’t wait to see him this morning at the Palais. I don’t regret it at all [having changed teams to be able to experience this].”

headline: Coquard: "It is a great finish"
subtext: Along with Mads Pedersen, Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) is the other rider in the peloton who has already won in Manosque: “It is a great finish, where I’ve already won [in the Tour de la Provence 2022]. We’re really keen and highly motivated today. I think that was my first year with Cofidis. I’d won the Étoile de Bessèges ahead of Pedersen the week before. It’s a tough, grueling finish – just the sort I like. The approach is a bit different from the Tour de Provence, with a demanding kilometre and sections at 7 per cent. It’s a slight uphill stretch, a little hill, where lactic acid builds up. It suits my strengths, so we’re keen to do really well today. [Van Aert and Pedersen’s ambitions] don’t change much. We’re ambitious too. They have more results than me in the Grand Tours, in La Vuelta, and recently, but I’ve prepared for La Vuelta as best I can. I think I’ll be in excellent form.”

headline: 60 kilometres to go
subtext: The gap is back up to 1'05''. The bonus sprint is 35.9 km from the finish.

headline: Kruijswijk ups the ante on an uphill section
subtext: And the gap rapidly drops to 30 seconds.

headline: Visma-Lease a Bike vs Hayter
subtext: Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) has accelerated at the front of the lead group. Behind them, Bruno Armirail takes over the pace setting in the bunch.

headline: Chumil has crashed
subtext: Race doctors are with the Guatemalan rider to see if he can continue in the race.

headline: Into the final 50 kilometres
subtext: The fap is down 12'' with just under 15 kilometres to go to the bonus sprint.

headline: Hayter goes solo at the front
subtext: With 49 kilometres to go, Bouwman, Fernandez and Uriarte trail by 5'', and the peloton by 20''.

headline: Chumil is the first rider out of La Vuelta 26
subtext: Sergio Chumil (Burgos Burpellet BH) couldn't resume racing after his crash.

headline: 10 kilometres to go to the sprint
subtext: Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) has pushed his lead back up to 25 seconds.

headline: Hayter resists
subtext: The British rouleur has a lead of 30'' with 5 kilometres remaining to the intermediate sprint. He eyes the bonus seconds awarded on the line to take a decisive step towards La Roja.

headline: Hayter takes 6 bonus seconds
subtext: The bonus seconds at the finish won't be enough for sprinters like Wout van Aert to try and take La Roja from the British powerhouse.

headline: Hayter is caught
subtext: Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) is at the very front of th peloton with 34 kilometres to go.

headline: Into the final 30 kilometres
subtext: Visma-Lease a Bike are still at the helm.

headline: Hayter at the back of the peloton
subtext: So far, so good for the British powerhouse. If he finishes in the same time as the winner, only Tadej Pogacar can be ahead of him in the overall standings. The Slovenian would need to finish first, with Hayter third at best, or second, with Hayter outside of the top 3.

headline: Results of the bonus sprint
subtext: 1. Hayter, 20 pts / 6’’ 2. Van Aert, 17 pts / 4’’ 3. Coquard, 15 points / 2’’ 4. Laporte, 13 pts 5. Tarling, 10 pts

headline: 20 kilometres to go
subtext: The tension is rising ahead of the finale.

headline: Many trains at the front of the peloton
subtext: Visma-Lease a Bike, UAE Emirates XRG, Lidl-Trek, Groupama-FDJ United, Netcompany Ineos... These teams make the most of the width of the road to position their leaders at the front ahead of the final 10 kilometres.

headline: A brutal pace inside the last 10 kilometres
subtext: Visma-Lease a Bike want to make it a hard run in into Manosque.

headline: 5 kilometres to go
subtext: Kern Pharma move up. This morning, Urko Berrade said the Spanish team want to sprint with Marc Brustenga today: "This uphill finale suits himvery well."

headline: The road rises
subtext: NSN set the pace on the uphill sections leading to the final kilometre.

headline: Van Aert attacks with 2 km to go
subtext: Pogacar tries to follow the Belgian!

headline: Last kilometre
subtext: Alessandro Romele has joined Wout van Aert and Tadej Pogacar.

headline: Matthew Brennan wins stage 2 of La Vuelta 26!
subtext: Tadej Pogacar appears to finish 3rd.

headline: Top 5
subtext: 1. Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) 2. Pau Miquel (Bahrain Victorious) 3. Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) 4. Mads Pedersen (Lidl-Trek) 5. Hugo Hofstetter (NSN)

headline: Hayter was dropped, Pogacar keeps La Roja
subtext: The provisional GC top 5: 1. Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) 2. Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike), +9'' 3. Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike), +10'' 4. Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM), +12'' 5. Finn Fisher-Black (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), +14''
